title: Design System: Modern Furniture Co. Analytics

display.purpose: The page title. One per page.

headline.purpose: KPI figures; blue for the good signal, red for a problem count, a dash when missing. 24px in narrow columns.

body.purpose: Captions, legends, list labels, KPI sub-lines, loading, empty and error messages.

body-chat.purpose: Chat answers, questions, composer and starter questions; 16px inputs on phones.

label.purpose: Mono uppercase KPI labels, units, Signals tags. 11px (--text-meta) is the product-wide size floor; tool steps use it without uppercase.

data.purpose: Mono values with tabular numerals beside ranked bars; chart ticks use the mono face at the 11px floor.

small.purpose: The chat footnote and a chart card's fallback reason; in mono for chat table cells and SQL, to fit the 440px column.

motion.name: ease-arrive
motion.purpose: The one easing for everything that arrives.

motion.name: chart-enter
motion.purpose: First draw of a chart: lines write in left to right, once.

motion.name: chart-update
motion.purpose: Data change (filter): marks morph to new values instead of redrawing.

motion.name: stale-dim
motion.purpose: Previous data stays visible but dimmed while a filter change loads.

motion.name: bar-slide
motion.purpose: Ranked bars slide to new lengths.

motion.name: drawer-in
motion.purpose: Chat column arrives from the side it docks on; closes instantly.

motion.name: fade-in
motion.purpose: New chat messages; also the reduced-motion entrance for the chat.

motion.name: pulse-running
motion.purpose: Running chat tool step; off under reduced motion.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Charts update without animation, bars jump, chat fades only; opacity and colour feedback remain.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: Gutter 16 to 24px; filters stop filling the row.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: Gutter 36px; the chat docks as a 440px column (below, a full-screen dialog).

breakpoints.name: @2xl (container)
breakpoints.purpose: KPIs 3 columns, Signals 2, compact panels 2 (third spans the row).

breakpoints.name: @5xl (container)
breakpoints.purpose: KPIs 6 columns; orders and revenue charts side by side at 2:1.

narrative.overview:
The system behaves like a well-kept ledger: ruled, exact and accountable. Every figure sits on a clean white page inside a hairline rule, and nothing on the page is allowed to be louder than the numbers it carries. Colour is a pen, not paint. Signal Blue records the main line of the story (the primary series, the leading item, the one action that matters). Alarm Red is the correction pen, used only where something went wrong. Everything else is graphite and paper.

The mood is calm, exact and accountable. The canvas is a cool, barely tinted grey with white panels resting on it, and depth comes only from tone and 1px rules, never from shadows. A single dark ink strip (Signals) is where the system speaks in sentences. Type pairs a sturdy grotesque for reading with a monospace for anything measured or machine-produced, so a reader can tell at a glance what is prose and what is a reading off the instrument. It is a single page with no navigation chrome: a small ink brand mark sits beside the title, and the data gets the full width.

Motion follows the same discipline. When a filter changes, the ledger re-writes itself: lines morph from the old values to the new ones so the reader sees what moved, stale numbers dim while fresh ones load, and nothing replays an entrance for show. The layout narrows gracefully when the chat column opens beside it, and it is never covered on a desktop.

Confirmed rejection: vivid gradient-heavy "AI dashboard" styling (neon gradients, glowing cards, gradient fills). The owner rejected an early version as looking vibe-coded, and the system exists in deliberate contrast to it.
keyCharacteristics: Flat white panels on a cool grey page, separated by 1px hairlines; zero shadows.
One accent (Signal Blue) and one warning (Alarm Red), each with a single job.
Hanken Grotesk for reading, IBM Plex Mono for measured values, labels and system output.
A single dark ink strip for plain-English findings computed from the data.
Charts drawn like annotations that morph, not redraw, when the data changes.
One page, no navigation; layout driven by the width of the content column, not the window.

rules.name: The Alarm Means Something Rule
rules.body: Alarm Red appears only where something went wrong. It is never decoration, never a brand colour, never a second accent. If a screen has no problem to report, it has no red.

rules.name: The First-in-Rank Rule
rules.body: In a ranked list only the leader gets Signal Blue. Everything else is Bar Grey, and only the worst item may turn red when ranking profit or performance, and only when there is more than one item.

rules.name: The One Dark Strip Rule
rules.body: Ink as a surface is reserved for the Signals findings. One dark strip per screen, at most.

rules.name: The Edge-You-Can-See Rule
rules.body: Containers may use the faint Hairline; anything you can click, type into or choose from uses Control Line (3:1). The two must never be swapped.

rules.name: The Mono Means Measured Rule
rules.body: IBM Plex Mono is for things that are measured or machine-produced: labels, ticks, values, tool steps, SQL. Never set prose or headlines in mono.

rules.name: The Big Number Rule
rules.body: A KPI figure is the largest text inside its card and sits directly under its mono label, with a one-line plain-English sub-line under it. Nothing else in the card competes with it.

rules.name: The Narrow-Gracefully Rule
rules.body: Nothing may set a width that stops the main column from shrinking. The page makes room for the chat; on a desktop the chat never covers the page.

rules.name: The No-Orphan Rule
rules.body: Column counts are chosen per group so items divide evenly at every width: six KPIs go 2 / 3 / 6, three panels go 1 / 2 (+ full row) / 3.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat. If something needs to stand apart, change its tone or give it a rule. Never add a shadow, glow or blur.

dos: **Do** keep every surface flat: tone (#f3f4f6 → #ffffff → #0e1621) and 1px rules carry all depth.
**Do** give each screen exactly one solid Signal Blue (#2b59ff) action.
**Do** reserve Alarm Red (#d92d3a) for things that went wrong, so red always means a problem.
**Do** border every interactive control with Control Line (#868e9a) and every container with Hairline (#e3e6eb).
**Do** set measured values, labels, ticks and system output in IBM Plex Mono, and sentences in Hanken Grotesk.
**Do** pair every chart colour with a second cue (solid, dashed or dotted lines, labels on marked points, legends, printed values), so colour never carries meaning alone.
**Do** give every chart a spoken summary and every data panel its loading, error, empty and updating states.
**Do** let charts morph between data states, and respect reduced motion.
**Do** size grids by the content column (container queries), so the page reflows the same way for a phone and for an open chat.
donts: **Don't** use vivid gradients, neon glows or gradient-filled cards. This look was explicitly rejected.
**Don't** add shadows, blurs or glows to any surface, at rest or on hover.
**Don't** use Alarm Red decoratively or as a second brand colour.
**Don't** add a second dark surface; the Ink strip is reserved for Signals.
**Don't** put Ok Green (#1f8a4c) on small text; it is for icons only.
**Don't** set prose or headlines in monospace, or measured values in the grotesque.
**Don't** add navigation for pages that do not exist.
**Don't** replay a chart's entrance animation on a data update, or animate anything for show.
**Don't** float the chat over the dashboard on desktop widths.
